TRIGGER_PATTERN: Sector ETF prediction where the model identifies a same-day two-sided macro catalyst (ISM Services) and refuses to pre-score it, futures are flat (ES +0.13% / NQ +0.16%), and the sector has a live negative single-ticker catalyst (AVGO −3% to −6% AHR) that the model explicitly refuses to let set the sector down — the model scores S0=S1=S2=S4=0, S3=−1, predicts flat/flat, but the actual session delivers a broad-market rip (+1.05% SPY) on the ISM Services beat, producing XLK +1.29% absolute / +0.24% relative that the flat band misses entirely. The model's two-sided-catalyst refusal and single-ticker veto combine to suppress both the up path (macro beat) and the down path (AVGO), leaving only flat when the market was going to move on the catalyst regardless of direction.

CURRENT_BEHAVIOR: When a same-day two-sided macro catalyst (ISM Services) is identified, the model refuses to pre-score it (S0=0) and treats it as a reason to cap magnitude at flat/mild. When a live negative single-ticker catalyst (AVGO −3% to −6% AHR) is present, the model refuses to let it set the sector down (single-ticker veto) and also refuses to treat it as a dampener on the up path. The combination produces S0=S1=S2=S4=0 with only S3=−1 (crowding), yielding flat/flat. The model treats "two-sided" as "no information" rather than "high variance with direction unresolved until the print." The model also treats the single-ticker veto symmetrically — it blocks AVGO from setting XLK down but does not recognize that a mega-cap-heavy sector with one large red name can still rally hard on a macro catalyst if the other mega-caps (NVDA/MSFT/AAPL) are green and the catalyst is risk-on.

CORRECTED_BEHAVIOR: When a same-day two-sided macro catalyst is identified AND the sector has a live single-ticker catalyst that is market-negative, the model should recognize that the two-sided catalyst creates elevated absolute-move risk in BOTH directions, and the flat band is the least likely outcome if the catalyst resolves with any conviction. Specifically: (1) A two-sided macro catalyst with a consensus forecast (~54.3 ISM) and a market that has sold off 3d (−1.89% rel) has asymmetric upside risk — a beat produces a short-covering rip in the most-crowded-short sector (semis #1 at 53% long but off from 82%, meaning recent sellers are underweight and will chase). (2) The single-ticker veto should apply to the DOWN path only when the negative name is not confirmed by breadth/leaders; it should NOT suppress the UP path when the macro catalyst is risk-on and the other mega-caps are green. (3) When S3=−1 (crowding) is the only negative and the macro catalyst is two-sided, the crowding factor should be treated as fuel for a short-covering rally on a beat, not as a persistent lid. (4) The model should assign a minimum magnitude band of mild (not flat) whenever a two-sided macro catalyst with consensus forecast is scheduled, because the flat band requires BOTH the catalyst to be a non-event AND the single-ticker negative to transmit — a conjunction that is less likely than either single path. (5) When the model's own Channel 2 text says "real two-sided event risk" and "do not write 'no macro print,' do not pre-score a miss," it should translate that into a wider predicted band (flat-to-up or flat-to-down with the direction conditional on the print), not a flat point estimate.

EVIDENCE: XLK actual +1.29% vs SPY +1.05% (rel +0.24%) on 2026-09-03. ISM Services beat (~54.3 consensus, actual beat) produced a broad-market rip. AVGO's −3% to −6% AHR did NOT transmit through NVDA/MSFT/AAPL (all green), and XLK still rallied +1.29% absolute. The model's predicted flat/flat missed both direction (flat vs up) and magnitude (flat vs mild/notable). The model's own Channel 2 identified ISM Services as "real two-sided event risk" and "do not write 'no macro print,' do not pre-score a miss" — but then scored S0=0 and capped at flat, contradicting its own risk assessment. The 3d relative lag (−1.89%) meant XLK had already de-risked; the crowding factor (S3=−1) was the only negative and it became fuel for the rally when the macro catalyst was risk-on.

This Technology lesson adds the single-ticker veto interaction: AVGO's negative AHR was used to block the down path but also suppressed the up path, when it should have only blocked down (and even that was questionable given NVDA/MSFT/AAPL were green).

BACKWARD_CHECK: Applying this lesson backward: 2026-08-28 predicted up/flat vs XLK −1.55% (dir MISS, mag MISS). That session had no two-sided macro catalyst identified (the model was focused on AVGO AHR and NVDA/PCE). The lesson would not have changed that prediction because the trigger (two-sided macro catalyst + single-ticker negative) was absent. 2026-08-27 predicted up/mild vs XLK +3.16% (dir HIT, mag MISS — actual exceeded mild). That session had NVDA earnings catalyst and the model predicted up — the lesson's "wider band when catalyst scheduled" would have helped there too (up/mild should have been up/notable given the catalyst). 2026-08-21 predicted down/flat vs XLK +0.11% (dir MISS). No two-sided catalyst identified that morning. The lesson does not create false positives on these historical runs.

CONFLICT_CHECK: This lesson conflicts with the standing "single-ticker" lesson that says AVGO must not set XLK to down/notable while NVDA/MSFT/AAPL hold. The resolution: the single-ticker veto remains valid for the DOWN direction (AVGO alone should not force a down call), but it should not be extended to suppress the UP direction when a macro catalyst is risk-on and other mega-caps are green. This lesson also conflicts with the "two-sided catalyst = do not pre-score" heuristic — the correction is that "do not pre-score" should mean "do not commit to a direction," not "predict flat." The lesson refines both heuristics without overturning them. It also interacts with the 08-13 lesson (carried AI cluster + flat NQ → mild/flat cap) — that lesson was designed for no-catalyst mornings; when a two-sided macro catalyst is scheduled, the cap should be lifted to allow mild-to-notable in either direction.

FALSIFIER: This lesson would be falsified if a session with (a) a two-sided macro catalyst with consensus forecast, (b) a live single-ticker negative in the sector, and (c) flat futures produced an actual absolute move inside ±0.5% (flat band). It would also be falsified if the model applied the wider band and the catalyst resolved as a non-event (actual near consensus) with the sector staying flat — in that case the wider band would have been unnecessary but not harmful (the lesson only requires mild minimum, not notable). The lesson is also falsifiable if a two-sided catalyst morning with a single-ticker negative consistently produces flat outcomes in future samples, which would suggest the conjunction (catalyst non-event + single-ticker transmission) is more likely than either single path.

DIVERGENCE_VERDICT: none_flagged — the model's own divergence check was correct (leading Σ(S0–S3) = −1 vs S4 = 0, no fight), but the absence of divergence did not justify a flat point estimate when a two-sided macro catalyst was scheduled. The error was not in the divergence logic but in the magnitude-band selection: the model treated "no divergence" as "flat" rather than "direction unresolved, magnitude elevated."

ACTIVE_LESSON_REVIEW: The 08-14 lesson (AVGO AHR is not a fresh-positive) fired correctly — AVGO was indeed sold and the model did not treat it as positive. The 08-13 lesson (carried AI cluster + flat NQ → mild/flat cap) fired but was misapplied: it capped magnitude at flat when the two-sided macro catalyst should have lifted the cap to mild minimum. The 08-28 lesson (mega-cap-over-macro-drag is open-session only, requires green mega-cap) was correctly applied to not forbid down, but the model did not recognize that the same logic (mega-caps green + macro catalyst) licensed up. The 08-10 lesson (oil-up inflation shock) was correctly idle. The 08-12 notable-up FAIL lesson was correctly applied (NQ +0.16% not ≥+0.5%). The open experiment (milder when |score|<4) contributed to the flat call but should not override the catalyst-elevated magnitude risk.
